scope: internal/middleware/asynqdl; explicit root insertion into active module audit. No live Redis or network services used.

findings.summary: Checking only retry counters omits dead-letter Insert/callback for first-attempt SkipRetry errors, even though Asynq archives them immediately.
findings.before: Actual worker metadata retried=0 maxRetry=5; Inspector observes archived; deadLetters=0 callbacks=0, expected1 each. Plain and wrapped sentinel both fail.

findings.summary: Final-attempt RevokeTask incorrectly inserts dead letter and invokes failure callback although Asynq deletes the task without archiving.
findings.before: Actual worker and Inspector observe task deleted; deadLetters=1 callbacks=1, expected0. Covers maxRetry0, after ordinary retry, wrapped RevokeTask, and errors.Join(SkipRetry,RevokeTask).

upstream_evidence.verified_semantics: handleFailedMessage checks errors.Is(RevokeTask) first and markAsDone; then retry exhausted OR errors.Is(SkipRetry) -> archive; otherwise retry. No internet assumptions.

fix: Match processor precedence: return original error immediately for wrapped RevokeTask; otherwise archive bookkeeping when wrapped SkipRetry or retry budget exhausted. Existing best-effort insertion/callback/error propagation remains.
regression_design: 11 table cases use actual Asynq Server plus isolated miniredis, enqueue via client with real worker task metadata and Inspector state verification. RetryDelayFunc holds ordinary error in Retry until inspected; Inspector.RunTask then delivers next attempt without sleeps or clock manipulation. Retention proves success becomes Completed while Revoke is deleted. Record FailCount and original error identity.
limits: Uses local miniredis rather than a production Redis server; Asynq worker scheduling, handler context and Inspector transitions are real.
No other middleware or all-router source audit claimed; router consumer tests were only executed.
Clone revision group remains separately frozen pending URL/child-offset interaction investigation.
